A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OneOcc, with matching core methods, datasets, and main experiments. The text, equations, tables, and figures support comparison. V1 ends after its references; v2 adds supplementary Sections 6–13.

before.justification: V1 reports original QuadOcc and Human360Occ benchmark results, retrained baseline comparisons, component ablations, lighting analyses, and runtime measurements in Sections 4.1–4.5.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds experiments on projection choices, calibration robustness, temporal aggregation, resolution, field of view, and embedded-device runtime.

M1.justification: The core DP-ER, BGV, GDC, AMoE-3D architecture and loss remain unchanged. Section 6.7 adds evaluated three-frame extensions using pose-aligned feature averaging or BEVFormer-style temporal attention. The new explanation of bilinear lifting clarifies a procedure already specified in v1's equations.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same QuadOcc and H3O datasets and occupancy tasks. V2 extends test conditions through restricted-field-of-view inputs and controlled calibration perturbations. The KITTI tables document configuration adaptations; they do not establish an additional evaluated benchmark.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the main benchmark tables is unchanged. Table 12 adds pose-aligned temporal averaging and BEVFormer-style temporal attention as comparative alternatives to single-frame OneOcc. Section 11 primarily documents existing baseline adaptations rather than establishing changes to those retained comparators.

E3.justification: V2 adds substantial experimental protocols: evaluation-only panorama cropping, expert and grid configurations, resolution scaling, deterministic calibration perturbations and noise-augmented retraining, three-frame fusion, and nested spatial evaluation ranges. It also introduces INT8/FP16 Jetson profiling. Newly disclosed settings for retained benchmarks do not establish that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's cumulative component ablation and lighting comparison, v2 adds expert-count/routing, field-of-view, Cartesian/cylindrical-grid, projection-path, resolution, calibration-noise, and temporal-fusion analyses. GDC visualizations, distance-wise comparisons, and a rainy-dusk semantic failure case further examine mechanisms and failure conditions.

E5.justification: V2 newly states that baseline seeds are fixed and calibration perturbations are deterministic by seed and frame ID. Jetson timings are explicitly averaged over 100 runs after five warm-ups. Neither version reports accuracy confidence intervals, error bars, or multi-seed variability; an increase in repeated training runs is not established.

E6.justification: Tables 2–5 retain their scores, but v2 adds extensive results. Table 12 reports temporal-attention mIoU of 21.18/34.25 on QuadOcc/H3O-Heter, versus single-frame 20.56/32.23; Table 15 reports Jetson throughput of 13.64 FPS versus MonoScene's 10.20. Section 4.5 also changes allocated/reserved FP32 memory from 1.86/2.65 GB to 1.82/2.58 GB.

T1.justification: The core model equations remain unchanged. V2 adds mathematical specifications for annotation voting and confidence, the empty-vote mask and gated refinement, and density-based label acceptance in Sections 9–10. Section 6.2 also defines AET as mIoU multiplied by FPS. These extend formal specification without adding theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract qualifies the LiDAR claim: v1 says OneOcc beats popular LiDAR baselines, whereas v2 says it remains competitive with classical LiDAR baselines. The four-component method, two dataset contributions, and headline H3O performance claims otherwise retain their meaning.

C2.justification: V1's brief calibration limitation becomes a broader discussion of coarse-grid limits for manipulation, restricted real-world coverage, the humanoid sim-to-real gap, and single-frame motion limitations. V2 also interprets calibration robustness versus clean accuracy, temporal fusion versus deployment cost, and semantic failures under rare weather/layout combinations.

D1.justification: Sections 9–11 newly document sensor synchronization, annotation and dynamic-object handling, voxel refinement, simulator capture, metadata, baseline adaptations, optimizers, schedules, normalization, and losses. Sections 6 and 8 add profiling and deployment details. These are substantial disclosures, although some grid-bound descriptions conflict. The repository destination and future-release wording remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds references supporting implementation and supplementary discussion, including Point-MoE/Point-MoDE, FAST-LIO2, CARLA, open-vocabulary occupancy, and occupancy world models/flow. These broaden supporting context while leaving the main related-work narrative and central research positioning largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The main text receives limited clarifications and editorial changes. The supplement substantially expands explanations of retained components, dataset construction, and baseline adaptations, using question/setup/findings/takeaway sections and consistent per-method templates. It also develops the previously brief limitations and outlook into an extensive discussion.

P2.justification: V2 adds Figures 5–19 and Tables 6–26, including projection illustrations, annotation pipelines, dataset statistics, runtime breakdowns, failure cases, and configuration tables. Some displays re-express existing information, such as semantic frequencies from Tables 2–3. Main Tables 2 and 4 are also compressed/reformatted while retaining their results.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation and transparency: measured Jetson runtime replaces v1's Thor extrapolation, targeted ablations test central design choices, and detailed benchmark-construction and baseline documentation address major reproducibility gaps. Failure analyses and explicit applicability limits also improve the balance of the claims. Conflicting voxel bounds in Sections 9–11 and Figure 7's inconsistent resolution caption still require clarification, but the added evidence and documentation provide a substantial net quality improvement.
